req_desc: The product serves travellers searching for a place to stay plus hosts publishing one, as one application ...
The application makes no network call at run time to any outside service.
An anonymous visitor may browse, search, open a listing, read published reviews, read the terms page ...
Signup is open, any visitor may create a guest account, any signed-in account may create a host profile.
Four accounts are seeded: `guest@example.com`, `guest2@example.com`, `host@example.com`, `host2@example.com` ...
`POST /api/auth/signup` creates a guest account, returning a bearer token ...
`POST /api/auth/login` returns a bearer token for a seeded address with the corpus password ...
Every endpoint other than signup, login, health, the payment webhook refuses a request carrying no bearer token.
The search control carries three segments labelled `Where`, `When`, `Who`, over one submit.
Every search parameter lives in the address, so a copied address reproduces the same results.
Guests are counted as four separate classes: adults, children, infants, pets ...
`GET /api/listings` answers a conjunction of geography, availability, attributes, total price ...
Availability is answered inside the query, so a dense area returns a full page in one round trip.
Pagination is by opaque `cursor`, never by offset ...
Search renders four distinct states: no results, over-narrow filters, component unavailable, partial.
A map pin's label carries the total for the queried dates, never the nightly rate.
The booking panel itemises the whole price before the guest commits.
With no dates chosen the panel shows a from-price, showing no total.
The availability view carries three states per date, the third being bookable but not as an arrival.
Instant book confirms on authorisation, request to book creates a pending hold instead.
The cancellation policy, house rules, total, rating sit above the booking control.
The nightly subtotal sums each date's own price across the half-open range.
The length-of-stay discount reduces the nightly subtotal alone, never a fee, never a tax.
The cleaning fee is charged once per stay, identical on a two-night stay or a thirty-night stay ...
The guest service fee is a rate over the accommodation total.
Tax comes from a stored jurisdiction table, dropping to zero at a jurisdiction's exemption threshold.
The pricing steps run in one fixed order, producing named intermediate totals nobody displays.
Rounding is half up, away from zero, at every multiplication, so displayed lines sum exactly to the displayed total.
A quote pins its inputs for a lifetime read from `QUOTE_TTL_SEC`, being consumed once.
A stay is a half-open range of local dates, so the third to the fifth is two nights ...
Simultaneous confirms for one listing over one range leave exactly one reservation stored ...
Six availability rules plus advance notice plus the availability window all gate a range.
An expired pending hold stops counting against availability with nothing having read the reservation ...
A reservation stores a copy of the cancellation policy, so a later policy edit leaves the terms unchanged.
The refund quote is computed from the stored policy against the listing's local time, being shown before confirmation.
Checkout re-prices plus re-checks availability on arrival, surfacing any difference for fresh consent.
A replayed `Idempotency-Key` returns the original result, creating no second reservation, no second authorisation.
Five named checkout failures each have their own path, with an unwritable reservation voiding the authorisation.
Before confirming, the guest sees the charged currency named in words.
Request to book authorises at confirmation, capturing only on host acceptance.
Inventory is arbitrated before any authorisation is attempted.
Listing currency, display currency, settlement currency stay three separate values, with the rate stored on the reservation.
A payment needing an interactive challenge answers `requires_action`, holding inventory under a short deadline.
Payment events are applied by their own timestamps, idempotently on the event id, never by arrival order.
A payout follows the check-in date in the listing's timezone, becoming eligible after a hold period.
A partial refund is computed from the policy snapshot, itemised, stored.
`/trips` groups reservations as upcoming, current, past.
Contact details in a message before confirmation are redacted on the server, on write plus on read.
A wishlist item stores the listing plus the dates the listing was saved under.
Neither review is published until both are submitted or the window closes ...
Rating aggregates count published reviews only, averaging six subratings independently.
Language, region, display currency are three independent account settings.
A listing's approximate circle is offset by a stored vector, stable across every visit ...
The accept-or-decline screen shows no guest photograph, no guest name.
Reservations, payments, payouts, refunds, cancellations are append-only, so a correction is a new row.
Unpublishing a listing leaves existing reservations untouched.
A calendar edit appears in the row at once, reverting with a message naming the field on a failed save.
A late imported block over confirmed nights raises a conflict for a person, auto-cancelling nothing.
Accepting a request captures the authorisation, declining voids the authorisation, freeing the nights.
`/host/earnings` lists scheduled payouts, released payouts, outstanding recoveries.
The home route title reads Havenn, a vertical bar, then Holiday rentals, cabins, beach houses & more ...
The link grid is headed `Inspiration for future getaways`, carrying six named tabs plus `Show more` ...
An unknown address renders the not-found view carrying `Oops!`, `Error code: 404`, seven named links ...
A terms page at `/terms` is reachable from every footer, linked from the signup form.
Twenty-three routes exist exactly as the route table names them.
An anonymous visitor opening a protected route is sent to sign-in, returning afterwards to the requested route ...
The search-then-reserve journey ends with the reservation under `/trips` plus the nights gone from availability ...
Every list carries an empty state naming what would fill the list.
The subject, a place to stay, is the first thing seen on every browsing surface.
Surfaces where a guest is deciding stay still, with nothing moving during the decision.
The palette is stated by role, with three meaning-carrying colours used for nothing else.
The brand colour belongs to the search submit alone, appearing far less often than the ink ...
One size carries the whole interface, with heaviness plus colour doing the work size variation would.
Elevation grows in spread, never in darkness, with the flattest step an inset hairline.
Triggered movement settles the way a weighted object settles, sharing one house overshoot ...
Every control carries resting, pointed-at, pressed, focused, unavailable states, with unavailable never signalled by colour alone ...
Body text meets the WCAG AA contrast bar, with the secondary grey never used below body size ...
At a narrow viewport nothing overflows sideways, with every navigation target still reachable ...
The home route, the search results, the listing detail arrive as server-rendered markup ...
The application reaches exactly one backing service, `postgres`, at `DATABASE_URL`.
`GET /api/health` returns `200` once the application is ready.
Every public route carries a distinct title plus a distinct description ...
`PENDING_HOLD_TTL_SEC` plus `QUOTE_TTL_SEC` are read from the environment at run time.
No price arithmetic happens in the browser, the breakdown renderer displaying a server-computed quote.
A just-booked listing still in the index opens with an honest message rather than a checkout failure.
Twenty-three tables exist, with every timestamp in UTC plus every stay date local to the listing.
The seeded password `deku-demo-pw-2026` works at login for every seeded account.
`listing` carries an `inventory_type`, a room type, a capacity, an IANA timezone, a currency, a status.
`calendar_day` holds one row per listing per open local date, carrying availability plus price plus stay bounds.
At most one reservation whose status is `pending` or `confirmed` covers any night of any listing.
A payment stores no card number, no security code, no bank detail in any column ...
A review row whose `published_at` is empty is readable only by the author.
Four listings are seeded: `Cedar Loft`, `Harbour Cottage`, `Kite House`, `Salt Marsh Cabin` ...
Changing one radius token moves every surface reading the radius token ...
Six settles are declared as a mass, a stiffness, a damping, so adding a seventh takes three numbers ...
The only scrubbed movement is the header's compact transition, with the results grid attaching no per-row animation.
Hover styles apply only where a pointer exists, so a tap leaves no control stuck looking hovered.
One visually-hidden idiom clips every description meant to be announced rather than seen.
Every icon is drawn in the page, with no icon font shipped.
The four category tabs read `All`, `Homes`, `Experiences`, `Services`, in a generously rounded pill form.
The listing card carries photo, wishlist heart, title, meta, dates, price, rating.
Both error routes carry no header, no footer, no chrome, with the display line the largest type in the product.
Every generated image is deterministic, so rebuilding twice produces identical bytes.
The application is single tenant, with one set of listings, no organisations ...
The application is reachable at `APP_PUBLIC_URL`, with the port mapping `${APP_PUBLIC_PORT}:4173` ...
A plain list endpoint returns a top-level JSON array, the search endpoint returning an object carrying a cursor ...
The reservation, the payment, the payout, the review are real rows in `postgres`.
